calls.reason: The first hands-on review of the December 2024 Sora, reported by TechCrunch, found objects vanishing and reappearing, like other tools. OpenAI admitted unrealistic physics, and the VideoPhy benchmark found broad physics failures across leading models.

Independent studies show the generalization weakness persisted: SCAN (2018) found RNNs failing at systematic composition, and Apple's 2024 GSM-Symbolic found reasoning brittle. The 2023 Nature result shows progress on some tasks, not that the problem was solved.

The Gemini comparison is mixed: a tiny gain on MMLU-Pro but about 11 points on HiddenMath. OpenAI's own o1 figures show a large AIME jump inside the 18-month window, so the overall 'incremental' claim is contested, not clearly settled.

OpenAI's o1 system card confirms hallucinations persisted, but nothing in the packet backs the 97% figure. Waymo's limited US footprint is only context, and the home humanoid pages could not be retrieved.

By late 2024 there was evidence of a data limit: Epoch AI projected the usable human-text supply would run out by 2026–2032, and the Consent in Crisis audit found sharply rising web data restrictions. The model-collapse paper qualifies this but doesn't refute it.
